title: Detailed visual similarities in organisms imply intrinsic randomness

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Detailed visual similarities in organisms imply intrinsic randomness

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Detailed visual similarities between members of the same species, and between the two symmetric sides of a system, in features that look complex and random cannot be attributed to environmental or initial-condition randomness and must come from intrinsic randomness generation.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And instead, there is no choice but to conclude that the randomness must in fact come from the mechanism of intrinsic randomness generation that I have discovered in simple programs, and discussed in this section.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “The Intrinsic Generation of Randomness” (from p. 315), p. 326. Scope: complex-looking patterns in physical, biological and other systems, especially bilaterally symmetric ones

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.33

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Similarity and apparent randomness require substantial choices of features and null models. Public images permit restricted comparative tests, but they rarely include developmental histories or controlled environmental and initial-condition variation. Observational similarity alone cannot establish that intrinsic deterministic randomness is the only possible source.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify within-organism bilateral similarity and within-species recurrence of fine-scale pattern features, then compare likelihoods under shared developmental noise, environmental noise, and deterministic instability models. A reproducible excess uniquely predicted by deterministic intrinsic generation would support the claim; successful stochastic alternatives would refute its necessity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The universal necessity language spans poorly sampled physical and biological systems.

Intrinsic and stochastic developmental mechanisms can produce the same pattern statistics.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Image archives are sufficient to test the negative half, that fine-scale agreement is too strong for independent environmental noise, for some well-photographed organisms. They do not cover the stated range of physical and biological systems, and a positive match is also what any shared deterministic program would produce. The claim is therefore testable only in part and only against the environmental-noise rival.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify within-species and left-right similarity for features that pass standard randomness tests, and compare that similarity with independent environmental noise. Excess bilateral or within-species agreement would reject ongoing environmental noise; agreement alone would not identify one intrinsic mechanism among other shared deterministic growth rules.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shared genes or shared developmental history produce matching patterns without the specific intrinsic-randomness mechanism.

Which features count as complex and random has to be fixed before the similarity test is meaningful.
